articles.title: Council Votes on Senior Exercise Class After Long Debate
articles.deck: Residents of Lower Millrace filled the hall on Monday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings. Celia Fontaine, who has lived in Lower Millrace for 20 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

The plan calls for senior exercise class along Cooper Street, with work expected to start in November. The Lower Millrace Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Zelda Alvarez, 64, Church Organist
articles.deck: Friends remember Zelda Alvarez for the many years of service to Tannery Flats.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Millrace Youth Center in his or her name. Zelda Alvarez died in July at home on Lilac Street, at the age of 64.
Born in Tannery Flats in the years after the war, Zelda Alvarez spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Tannery Flats.

articles.title: Millrace Middle School Students Earn Regional Honors
articles.deck: The program begins in April and is open to all students in grade 7 and up.
body: Principal Wanda Bruckner said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. Students will meet on Monday afternoons in St. Brendan’s hall, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
The board will review the results at the end of the fall term. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for April.

articles.title: Then & Now: Millrace Green, 1985 and 2010
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1985 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Orion Avenue from the corner of Oak Street.

Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height. Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.
A 1985 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Orion Avenue from the corner of Oak Street.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Street Tree Planting
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. Please keep the street tree planting in the budget. Many of us on Grove Street use it every week.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the May meeting.
Vera Ashby, Mill Hill

articles.title: Council Approves $7,500 for Cooper Street Repairs
articles.deck: The vote came after 7 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 7 weeks once it starts in September. Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: The Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group Hosts Senior Exercise Class on Tuesday
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: The event will be held at the Eastgate community hall, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Tuesday. Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.
Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: Letter: the Millrace Youth Center Did a Good Job This Winter
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

Please keep the basketball court in the budget. Many of us on Dover Place use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Dover Place for 6 years, and I want to say what a difference the Millrace Youth Center has made.
Bernadette Vance, Upper Commons
